paper_metadata.title: QEA-FAD: Quantum Enhanced Autoencoders For Anomaly Detection in Finance and Healthcare

experiments.description: Breast cancer anomaly detection using the proposed QEA-FAD first ansatz with dual encoders, amplitude/angle embedding, and two CNOT links between encoder latent and trash qubits; evaluated in Qiskit simulation and on IBM QPU hardware.

algorithm.ansatz: dual variational quantum autoencoder with amplitude embedding in the first encoder and angle embedding in the second encoder

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) features are encoded into quantum states; paper states a 7-qubit architecture example with q0-q5 as latent qubits and q6 as trash qubit, and also reports experiments using all 32 features or top 8 features.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Train the autoencoder on normal/benign data to maximize reconstruction fidelity and separate benign from malignant samples by compression fidelity thresholding.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraint formulation reported; anomaly detection is performed by fidelity thresholding on trash qubits.

problem_instance.description: Breast cancer diagnosis anomaly detection on the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) dataset.

dataset_specification.description: 569 samples; 30 original numerical features plus two engineered features ('under average' and 'over average') for a total of 32 features; experiments also used the top 8 most relevant features for efficiency.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Two additional features were engineered to represent deviations beyond two standard deviations; no further preprocessing details reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compression fidelity histograms and loss over epochs; threshold-based classification using split value 0.845; comparison of Qiskit simulation and IBM QPU results.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compression fidelity thresholding with split value 0.845 to classify benign vs malignant samples.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical speedup claim reported for this experiment.

experiments.description: Breast cancer anomaly detection using the proposed QEA-FAD first ansatz on IBM QPU hardware, evaluated via compression fidelity and SWAP-test-style hardware inference.

algorithm.variant: QEA-FAD proposed dual-encoder quantum autoencoder on hardware
algorithm.ansatz: dual variational quantum autoencoder with amplitude embedding in the first encoder and angle embedding in the second encoder

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same breast cancer feature encoding as the simulation experiment; latent/trash qubit split used for anomaly detection.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize reconstruction fidelity for benign samples and separate malignant samples by lower compression fidelity.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Fidelity-based anomaly detection; no explicit mathematical constraints reported.

problem_instance.description: Breast cancer diagnosis anomaly detection on the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) dataset.

dataset_specification.description: 569 samples; 32 features after augmentation; top 8 features also mentioned as an efficiency setting.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Two engineered features added; no further preprocessing details reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of inference compression fidelity on IBM QPU hardware versus simulation; threshold-based classification using split value 0.845.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compression fidelity thresholding with split value 0.845.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical speedup claim reported for the hardware experiment.

experiments.description: Credit card fraud anomaly detection using the e2 quantum autoencoder on the public fraud dataset, evaluated in simulation and on IBM Guadalupe and Rigetti Aspen-11 hardware.

algorithm.variant: e2 quantum autoencoder for fraud detection

problem_formulation.encoding_method: amplitude_encoding and/or angle_embedding not explicitly distinguished for this experiment
problem_formulation.encoding_details: Credit card transaction features are embedded into the quantum circuit; the paper states the e2 encoder was trained on the credit card dataset and evaluated by compression fidelity separation between fraudulent and non-fraudulent transactions.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Train on non-fraudulent transactions to maximize compression fidelity for normal data and minimize fidelity for fraudulent data.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Fidelity-based anomaly detection; no explicit constraints reported.

problem_instance.description: Fraud detection on the Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset.

dataset_specification.description: 284,807 transactions; 492 fraudulent and the rest non-fraudulent; 30 PCA-derived features plus Time and Amount are mentioned in the dataset description.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Features are PCA-derived; Time indicates elapsed seconds between transactions and Amount indicates transaction value.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compression fidelity comparison between fraudulent and non-fraudulent transactions; simulator results and hardware results on IBM Guadalupe and Rigetti Aspen-11 are reported.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Best parameters from training the e2 encoder were used for hardware inference.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical baseline or speedup claim reported; hardware results are compared qualitatively to simulator results.
